extracted.intended_audience: software developers and teams using GitHub for pull-request-based code review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing and organizing code reviews on GitHub using pull requests, diffs, inline comments, reviewer requests, branch protections, and status checks to improve code quality and collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pull requests as the unit of change
rubrics_metrics.description: Every change starts with a pull request. Start a new feature or propose a change to existing code with a pull request — a base for your team to coordinate details and refine your changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pull requests are fundamental to how teams review and improve code on GitHub. Use them to evolve projects, propose new features, and discuss implementation details before changing your source code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preview changes with diffs in context
rubrics_metrics.description: Diffs: Preview changes in context with your code to see what is being proposed. Side-by-side Diffs highlight added, edited, and deleted code right next to the original file, so you can easily spot changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the diff view to quickly identify additions, edits, and deletions and to understand the intent of a change before commenting or merging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the pull request history/timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: History: Browse commits, comments, and references related to your pull request in a timeline-style interface. Your pull request will also highlight what’s changed since you last checked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the timeline to follow discussion, see commit progression, and focus review on new or updated changes since your last review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use blame to trace file evolution and authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Blame: See what a file looked like before a particular change. With blame view, you can see how any portion of your file has evolved over time without viewing the file’s full history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use blame to identify who introduced lines of code and understand historical context when assessing a change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment inline and discuss code alongside changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments: On GitHub, conversations happen alongside your code. Leave detailed comments on code syntax and ask questions about structure inline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make comments specific to the code lines in question and ask clarifying questions or suggest improvements directly where they apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request reviewers to get timely feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Review requests: If you’re on the other side of the code, requesting peer reviews is easy. Add users to your pull request, and they’ll receive a notification letting them know you need their feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add the right teammates or teams as reviewers so they are notified and can prioritize the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bundle comments into coherent reviews and use review states
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews: Save your teammates a few notifications. Bundle your comments into one cohesive review, then specify whether comments are required changes or just suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a single review with a clear decision (approve, request changes, comment) and categorize feedback as required or optional to reduce notification noise and set reviewer expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub UI when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Merge pull requests faster by resolving simple merge conflicts on GitHub—no command line necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conflicts are straightforward, resolve them via the web interface to speed up merging; escalate complex conflicts for local resolution with the author as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use permissions to limit risk and grant appropriate access
rubrics_metrics.description: Give collaborators as much access as they need through your repository settings. You can extend access to a few teams and select which ones can read or write to your files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the principle of least privilege—grant read/write only to those who need it and use teams to manage access at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect branches to maintain code integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Protected Branches help you maintain the integrity of your code. Limit who can push to a branch, and disable force pushes to specific branches. Then scale your policies with the Protected Branches API.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable branch protection rules (e.g., restrict pushes, require PRs) to prevent accidental or unauthorized changes to important branches like main or release branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require status checks to block merges until checks pass
rubrics_metrics.description: Required status checks: Create required status checks to add an extra layer of error prevention on branches. Use the Status API to enforce checks and disable the merge button until they pass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configure CI/tests/lint checks as required status checks so changes cannot be merged until automated verification succeeds, reducing human error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage review tooling to improve code quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews can improve your code, but mistakes happen. Limit human error and ensure only high quality code gets merged with detailed permissions and status checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine manual review (comments, requested changes) with automated enforcement (status checks, protected branches, permissions) to raise overall code quality and reduce regressions.
